lectures.title: Panchayati Raj and urban local bodies

items: **Core principle:** an exercise in democratic decentralisation, community participation and local accountability (NOT central control or mere administration).
**Constitutional directive:** Article 40 (DPSP) directs the State to organize Village Panchayats as units of self-government.

**Functional domain:** Local Self-Government includes public health, sanitation, water supply and rural development; Maintenance of Public Order and Judicial Review are NOT local-government functions.
**Charles Metcalfe:** described Indian village communities as "Little Republics".
**Lord Ripon (1882 Resolution):** recognized as the Father of Local Self-Government in India.
**GoI Act, 1919:** Local Self-Government made a Transferred Subject under provincial dyarchy.
**Panchayati Raj first inaugurated:** 2 October 1959 in Nagaur district (Rajasthan) by Nehru.
**First Panchayati Raj State:** Rajasthan; Andhra Pradesh followed second.
**Madhya Pradesh:** first state to implement the 73rd Amendment in true spirit.
3-tier Panchayati Raj (Gram Panchayat -- Panchayat Samiti -- Zila Parishad); recognized as the Architect of Panchayati Raj
A 2-tier model and separate Nyaya Panchayats
Decentralisation of powers/finance and district planning bodies
Revitalization and representative character of Panchayats
Constitutional status and greater financial resources for local bodies

**Sequence:** 1957 Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (3-tier model) -- 2 Oct 1959 first launched in Nagaur, Rajasthan -- 1977 Ashok Mehta Committee -- 1985 G.V.K. Rao Committee -- 1986 L.M. Singhvi Committee.
**1996:** Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA).
Village: Gram Panchayat; Block: Panchayat Samiti; District: Zila Parishad
Transitional Area: Nagar Panchayat; Smaller Urban: Municipal Council; Larger Urban: Municipal Corporation

parts.t: Structure: Gram Sabha, tiers and composition
items: **Art. 243A (Gram Sabha):** village-level general assembly of all persons registered in the village electoral rolls.
**Gram Sabha vs Gram Panchayat:** Gram Sabha is the entire electorate (body of registered voters); Gram Panchayat is the elected executive body.
**Art. 243B (Three-Tier System & Exemption):** mandatory 3-tier structure; 3-tier Panchayati Raj applies everywhere.
The Intermediate tier (Panchayat Samiti) is **optional** in States with a population of **≤20 Lakhs**.
**Art. 243C & 243R (Composition):** the State Legislature regulates composition (for both Panchayats and Municipalities).

parts.t: Elections, minimum age, reservation and tenure
items: **Election:** Ward members/Panchs of Panchayats & Municipalities are directly elected by local voters; mode is Direct (Local Body framework).
**Minimum age:** 21 years to contest Panchayat / Municipality elections, NOT 25 or 30 years: Article 243F(1)(a) (Panchayats); Article 243V(1)(a) (Municipalities).
**Who it covers:** Panchayat Member / Chairperson; Municipality Member / Mayor. Disqualification does not apply if aged ≥ 21 (IAS Pre 2025 Trap).
**Art. 243D & 243T (Reservations):** mandatory reservation of not less than 1/3rd (≥33%) of total seats and chairpersons for women.
**Art. 243E & 243U (Tenure & Dissolution):** fixed term of 5 years; if dissolved prematurely, elections must be held within 6 months (not required if remaining term is < 6 months).
**Art. 243K & 243ZA (State Election Commission):** superintendence, direction and conduct of local elections; the SEC conducts elections.
**Art. 243G & 243W (Powers & Responsibilities):** powers over economic development, social justice, sanitation, public health, local utilities, and roads/bridges.
**Art. 243-I & 243-Y (State Finance Commission):** constituted every 5 years by the Governor to review local finance distribution.
**Art. 243J & 243Z (Accounts & Audit):** State Legislature provides for maintenance and audit of accounts.
**Audit authority:** Panchayat audit laws are enacted by the State Legislature (NOT the Union Parliament, CAG, or District Collector).

lectures.title: Governance: the Right to Information Act, 2005

items: **Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005:** a legal right supporting transparency/accountability.
**Roots and case:** rooted in the MKSS movement; Namit Sharma Case, 2012.
Assented on 15 June 2005; fully came into force after 120 days on 12 October 2005.
